title: Reusable WeightStack view (stack/unstack) for any ModelLayout
description: Lift site/src/experiments/mpnn/weights3d.ts into a reusable view taking a ModelLayout + optional trace focus. Decide home: it is raw WebGPU (not use.gpu); AGENTS says GPU/rendering belongs in viewer, and nn must stay renderer-free. Options: viewer export, nn ./view subpath, or site-only module. Acceptance: ProteinMPNN page uses it unchanged in behaviour; a second toy model (e.g. a 2-layer MLP built from NnRuntime) renders through the same view in a site test.
close_reason: Decision: WeightStack lives in the site (site/src/experiments/weights/weight-stack.ts): it is raw WebGPU, nn must stay renderer-free, and viewer is use.gpu-based. Takes stages of {name, shape, buffer?, values?, scale?}; ProteinMPNN page and the new #experiments/models (toy MLP created and run on the GPU, binding the same buffers) both use it; site test covers both. Branch feat/model-layout, thread T-01a21844-9cb6-7563-90e1-9d3565963c0a.

title: Model layout contract: renderer-free stages -> matrices for any NnRuntime model
description: Replace the site's ProteinMPNN name regexes with renderer-free, data-free ModelLayout stages in @molgpu/nn. The implemented API is generic layoutFromSteps(trace.steps, shapes), not ProteinMpnn.layout(); roles and GPU bindings are not part of the core layout. The site attaches buffers in its own adapter. Acceptance: every 2-D checkpoint weight appears exactly once in first-use order, and the site has no ProteinMPNN name parsing. Header-derived layouts use name heuristics, not verified forward order. Thread T-01a21844-9cb6-7563-90e1-9d3565963c0a.
close_reason: ModelLayout/LayoutStage/LayoutMatrix in @molgpu/nn with layoutFromSteps (from a trace; ProteinMPNN GPU test asserts every 2-D weight once, 9 stages in forward order) and layoutFromNames (header-only models). Site no longer parses ProteinMPNN names (forwardRank/groupOf removed). Branch feat/model-layout, thread T-01a21844-9cb6-7563-90e1-9d3565963c0a.

title: Sequence -> matrix mode: letters -> one-hot -> W_s rows -> h_S -> decoder -> P(aa)
description: Mode 2. Show native sequence as letters, the L x 21 one-hot, the W_s [21 x 128] rows each letter selects (labelled by amino acid), the resulting h_S, decoder layers with the visibility mask, and end on per-residue P(aa) letter bars synced with the 3D protein.
close_reason: View: Sequence -> P(aa): one-hot [L x 21] x W_s [21 x 128] (hovered letter lit) = h_S, + encoder h_V, decoder 1-3, W_out softmax -> P(aa); player limited to sequence/decoder/output. Merged in PR #112: https://github.com/zachcp/molgpu/pull/112.

title: Forward-pass view: left-to-right flow (sequence/backbone in, P(aa) out)
description: User request: lay the pass out left to right, inputs on the left and outputs on the right, instead of the current depth stack / column grid. Acceptance: unstacked and playback views read left-to-right in forward order; stage labels kept; site test asserts order.
close_reason: Weights3D stack viewed from -x so forward order runs left to right; focused slab lifts up; FlowPanel rows run input (left) to output (right). Merged in PR #112: https://github.com/zachcp/molgpu/pull/112.

title: Encoder-only mode: backbone -> neighbour graph -> structural embeddings on the protein
description: Mode 1. Show backbone atoms (N/CA/C/O), the hovered residue's K=48 neighbours drawn on the structure, its 25 atom-pair RBF distance features and positional classes, then per-layer h_V/h_E. Every frame tied to residues in 3D. No amino acids: the encoder sees only geometry.
close_reason: View: Encoder only (backbone): backbone-only spacefill coloured by hovered residue's neighbour rank; flow RBF [K x 25 pairs x 16] with neighbour labels and CA distances -> h_E -> encoder h_V 1-3; player limited to feature+encoder steps. Merged in PR #112: https://github.com/zachcp/molgpu/pull/112.

title: @molgpu/nn package: WGSL ops, ProteinMpnn with PyTorch parity
description: packages/nn: CPU reference ops + WGSL kernels, NnRuntime (raw WebGPU, owned/wrapped buffers), safetensors reader, ProteinMpnn encode/decode. GPU parity vs upstream PyTorch <=1.3e-4 log-prob on 1crn/1ema/1a4y (deno task test:nn:gpu). Merged in PR #112.
close_reason: Implemented and verified in thread T-01a21844-9cb6-7563-90e1-9d3565963c0a; merged in PR #112: https://github.com/zachcp/molgpu/pull/112.

title: ProteinMPNN model explorer: physical layout and forward pass on real data
description: Site experiment #experiments/mpnn plus @molgpu/nn (ProteinMpnn, ProteinMpnnTrace). Goal: show a protein flowing through the real in-memory weights, encoder through decoder to P(aa), with biologically legible steps. Thread T-01a21844-9cb6-7563-90e1-9d3565963c0a.

title: WeightStack for large models: GPU tile summaries of real weights
description: Remaining scope: compute GPU tile summaries (mean |w| per 32x32 block) for real weight matrices too large to bind directly, so a 4096x11008 matrix binds a small summary buffer. Acceptance: an executable value-backed WeightStack example checked against independently computed tile means, respecting maxStorageBufferBindingSize and bounded per-frame draw count. Header-only catalogs, shape-only slabs, FP4 logical shapes and compact layouts are already implemented in PR #113 and are not new work here.
notes:
Catalog now includes DeepSeek-V4-Pro (1.60T, 64 shards, I8 FP4 experts x384), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (763B), Kimi-K3 and K3.1-Pro (2.78T, 96 shards, U8 FP4 experts x896, vision tower). layoutFromNames collapses MoE copies (count), drops quant scales, unpacks FP4 shapes; catalog stores layouts (731 KB) not raw tensor lists. WeightStack draws experts as thicker slabs. Open: GPU tile summaries for real values of large matrices.
Earlier (feat/model-layout c182863): readSafetensorsHeader + safetensorsHeaderLength (two range requests per file); scripts/catalog_model_shapes.ts writes site/src/experiments/models/catalog.json (also ProteinMPNN, ESM-2 8M/650M, AMPLIFY 350M, BERT base, GPT-2, phi-2, Qwen2.5 0.5B/7B, Mistral 7B; sharded via index.json). WeightStack draws shape-only slabs at true proportions, caps stack depth, wraps the grid into rows; local .safetensors open uploads values up to 256 MiB and the per-matrix binding limit, else header only.

title: Spike: per-residue substitution matrix view (ProteinMPNN / MSA profiles)
description:
Goal: visualize per-position amino-acid distributions (L x 20/21) on structure,
e.g. ProteinMPNN conditional log-probs, MSA position-specific frequencies/PSSM,
or ESM masked-marginal scores (deep mutational scan-like L x 20 matrices).

Questions the spike should answer:
- Data contract: renderer-free L x 20 value with alphabet order, units
  (log-prob, probability, delta vs wild type) and provenance; per-residue
  reductions (entropy, wild-type probability, top substitution) exposed as
  residue-domain attributes for ordinary coloring.
- Views: (a) color structure by entropy / WT log-prob; (b) pick a residue ->
  show its 20-way distribution (logo or bar inset) anchored to the residue;
  (c) sequence-logo / heatmap strip linked to the 3D selection;
  (d) per-substitution coloring ("color by P(Ala)" or by delta for a chosen AA).
- Index mapping between designed/sequence positions and structure residues.

Outcome: decision + alternatives, an executable site experiment with a
precomputed ProteinMPNN (or PSSM) fixture for a small structure, and follow-ups.
Relates to the attention-on-structure spike (shared residue-indexed matrix
contract); no model inference here.
notes: PR #112 merged the live ProteinMPNN explorer with hover bars and P(aa) strips (molgpu-sept-6b3). Reuse that UI rather than rebuilding it. Remaining scope is a reusable residue-indexed contract with alphabet, units, provenance and residue mapping, plus a precomputed ProteinMPNN/PSSM/MSA example and any missing per-substitution views. Pairwise attention remains separate in molgpu-sept-zi9.

title: Spike: map attention heads / pairwise model statistics onto protein structure
description:
Goal: explore representations of pairwise (L x L) statistics from sequence models
on a 3D structure: transformer attention heads (e.g. ESM-2 per layer/head),
MSA-derived couplings (DCA/APC-corrected covariance), and predicted contact maps.

Questions the spike should answer:
- Data contract: where does an L x L (optionally layers x heads x L x L) matrix
  live? Candidate: a renderer-free value in `table` or `fields` keyed to residue
  rows, with provenance ("imported:esm2-t33" etc.) like existing attributes.
  Residue-domain per-residue reductions (row sums, entropy, max attention) can
  use the existing attribute path (`withAttributes`, `ATTRIBUTE_DOMAINS`).
- Representations to compare: (a) thresholded/top-k residue-pair lines or arcs
  between CA atoms, width/alpha by weight; (b) per-residue color from a chosen
  query residue (click/pick a residue -> color all others by attention to it);
  (c) linked 2D heatmap beside the 3D view with brushing both ways; (d) head/layer
  scrubbing via timeline or a slider.
- Mapping sequence index -> structure residues (gaps, missing residues, chains,
  tokenizer offsets like BOS/EOS).
- Scale: L=500 gives 250k pairs per head; decide CPU top-k vs GPU filtering.

Outcome: decision + alternatives, one executable site experiment
(site/src/experiments) on a small PDB with a precomputed attention/contacts
fixture, and bounded follow-up beads. No model inference in this spike.

title: Spike: pure-WebGPU ProteinMPNN whose weight buffers feed both inference and visualization
description:
Goal: run ProteinMPNN in the browser as WGSL compute on molgpu's own GPUDevice,
so the same GPUBuffers hold the real weights that the forward pass reads AND
that a weight/activation view samples. One owner per buffer, no CPU readback.

Findings (2026-11-26, thread T-01a21844-9cb6-7563-90e1-9d3565963c0a, artifact
"Pure-WebGPU ProteinMPNN: feasibility and routes"):
- No existing WebGPU MPNN exposes its weights. sokrypton/mpnn is CPU-only
  (JS + WASM SIMD) but is the best reference: small op set (linear, GELU,
  LayerNorm, gathers), encode-once/decode-many split, a flat fp16 .mpnn weight
  format (magic + JSON header + tensors), and a PyTorch parity suite
  (golden tensors, maxAbs ~3e-5 in fp32). Repo has no LICENSE file; weights
  are MIT (dauparas). Check licensing before reusing code.
- MurrellLab/webProteinMPNN runs ONNX bundles on onnxruntime-web WebGPU (MIT).
  ORT accepts our GPUDevice and keeps I/O on GPU (Tensor.fromGpuBuffer,
  preferredOutputLocation 'gpu-buffer'), but weights are opaque initializers
  and intermediate activations are unreachable without graph surgery.

Route A (matches the goal): load weights into viewer-owned GPUBuffers and port
the feature/kNN builder plus 3 encoder + 3 decoder layers to WGSL, following
the raw-WebGPU job pattern in gpu-dssp.ts (record the reason per AGENTS.md).
Frameworks surveyed (jax-js, tfjs WebGPU, @johnhenry/backend-webgpu, TypeGPU,
ORT, webgpu-torch, Rust/wasm): none fits molgpu's device and buffer ownership
better than extending internal/gpu-job.ts with ~8 kernels (kNN, RBF features,
linear+GELU, gather-concat, masked K-sum, residual LayerNorm, log-softmax,
Gumbel sampling). Use jax-js only as an optional per-op test oracle.
Route B (fallback): ORT WebGPU on the shared device for outputs only, plus a
separate weight copy for display.

Outcome: decision, an executable slice (feature builder + first encoder layer
in WGSL matching golden tensors within fp32 tolerance on a small PDB, with a
heatmap of that layer's weight buffer), and bounded follow-ups. The residue-indexed [L, 21] contract in molgpu-sept-kwx is related research, not a prerequisite for the already implemented inference path.
notes: PR #112 merged @molgpu/nn and the shared-buffer explorer (molgpu-sept-6b3.1/.2). This is no longer uncommitted work. The implementation owns buffers in NnRuntime, builds kNN/RBF features on the CPU, and reads probabilities/trace values back for UI diagnostics. Keep this spike in progress for a decision on the original GPU feature-building/no-readback requirements; do not repeat the existing inference kernels or close it as fully pure-WebGPU without resolving those requirements. Original feasibility findings above remain historical evidence.
